body.statement: Exactly one alternative holds for the oracle-instance \(\mathsf X_{\mathrm{phys}}\): either the feasible-case theorem returns \(E^{\star}\), or \(\operatorname{Opt}=+\infty\). The latter occurs if and only if \(\operatorname{Acc}(Q,E;G)=0\) for every uniform certificate of length at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\). Exhaustive enumeration decides the alternative in time \(2^{O(B_{\mathrm{cert}})}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})\), with one cached source-oracle reply per queried distinct protocol; there is no certificate or output-length term in the infeasible input.
body.justification: The explicit finite alternative makes infeasibility decidable without a polynomial-witness or full-incidence-compilation premise.
body.gap: Fixed-source CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) decides one supplied collection; it does not decide existence over all priced legal physical protocols while charging access to their support and source-law handles.
body.consumer: A planner can distinguish a costly but attainable reward-law query from one unattainable under the available catalogue.

obligation.what_is_open: The missing direction is that absence of an accepted certificate of length at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\) excludes every feasible generic acquisition.
obligation.obstruction: Only the unresolved uniform-source and canonical-certificate statements connect an arbitrary accepting collection to that bounded search space.
obligation.attempted: I proved the finite dichotomy and enumeration argument conditional on the canonical bound; there is no independent route from a failed bounded search to generic infeasibility in the frozen core.
obligation.partial_result: Conditional on the canonical-certificate lemma, feasibility is equivalent to the existence of an accepted certificate among the finitely many strings of length at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\).  If none is accepted, the feasible set in the definition of \(\operatorname{Opt}\) is empty and hence \(\operatorname{Opt}=+\infty\); if one is accepted, the alternatives are disjoint.  Exhaustive enumeration with cached replies has the stated exponential time, and in the negative case no output certificate length is charged.  The only missing implication is the unresolved reduction from an arbitrary accepting acquired collection to a bounded uniform certificate.
